title: Logitech G502 X Lightspeed Review: No lights, same price
summary: Logitech's G502 X Lightspeed strips the G502 X Plus of its lighting, but retains the $160 price tag.
body: Logitech's G502 X Lightspeed has been around for awhile — the mouse was introduced in 2022 alongside the fancier Logitech G502 X Plus (and the wired G502 X), but since it’s receiving a firmware update that upgrades its Hero 25K sensor to a Hero 44K sensor, this seemed like a good time to take a look at it. The G502X Lightspeed is available in black and white colorways and currently retails for $159.99, which is the same price as the G502 X Plus — however, it can (and should) normally be found for less than this. Design and Comfort of the G502 X Lightspeed The Logitech G502 X Lightspeed is a right-handed gaming mouse with an ergonomically contoured shape. It's the same size and shape as the G502 X Plus, with large primary mouse buttons, textured rubber side panels for grip, and a smooth matte chassis with glossy accents. It comes in black and white colorways (our review unit was black) and has no lighting aside from a small indicator light at the front of the mouse to indicate connection and battery life. title: The end of an era as Linux 7.5 purges the last 30-year-old Intel MMX optimizations from Pentium age
summary: Linux developers are preparing to make Intel’s ancient MultiMedia eXtensions irrelevant, with the last MMX code now set to be removed from the kernel.
body: Linux developers are preparing to make Intel’s ancient MultiMedia eXtensions an irrelevance. Intel introduced MMX in the Pentium era, but a patch expected to merge into mainline Linux 7.5 will remove the last remaining optimized software from the open-source OS. Expected to be released in 2027, the new kernel will wipe MMX-optimized code from its software RAID XOR code, explains Phoronix . Admittedly, there wasn’t much left in Linux in terms of MMX optimizations. But few folks will be running the most modern kernels on Pentium MMX and Pentium II chips in 2026. And most other MMX-optimized code disappeared from the OS half a decade ago, when some MMX-optimized memory management code was removed. Note that, if you are a determined late-90s Pentium devotee, you can still use software RAID, but it will lack the MMX fast path. This is a classic case of Linux code housekeeping. With this change, the kernel will lose over 800 lines of code and replace them with just 12. Remembering MMX Intel first introduced MMX Pentium chips in January 1997. body: "كان يعمل 12 ساعة يوميا"! اقترب موعد عودة المدير الفني البلجيكي فينسنت كومباني إلى مقاعد بدلاء بايرن ميونخ، وذلك وفقا لتصريحات أدلى بها أولي هونيس الرئيس الفخري للنادي البافاري. وسقط كومباني مغشيا عليه أثناء مشاهدة حصة تدريبية لفريق الشباب، ونُقل على الفور إلى المستشفى. ومنذ ذلك الحين، يتولى مساعده، آرون دانكس، مسؤولية النادي البافاري. وتبدو الأخبار الواردة من ميونخ إيجابية للغاية، فقد كشف أولي هونيس، الرئيس الفخري لنادي بايرن ميونخ، أن كومباني سينضم إلى الفريق مجددا بعد انتهاء فترة التوقف الدولي. ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة وأوضح في تصريح لشبكة "BR24" نقلته صحيفة سبورت الإسبانية، الأحد: "سيعود إلينا في غضون أسبوعين أو ثلاثة أسابيع. لذا بعد فترة التوقف الدولي، سيعود إلى مقاعد البدلاء. لقد كان يعمل اثنتي عشرة ساعة في اليوم، ستة أيام في الأسبوع: كان ذلك ببساطة أكثر من اللازم". وعلقت الصحيفة الإسبان "كان لهذه الكلمات أثرا أكثر طمأنينة بكثير من تلك التي أدلى بها المدير الرياضي ماكس إيبرل بعد فوز السبت على ماينز، حيث قال: " فيني (كومباني) يتقدم بشكل جيد في تعافيه. ومع ذلك، لا يزال يتعين علينا انتظار الضوء الأخضر من الأطباء قبل السماح له بالعودة". وإذا صدقت توقعات هونيس، فقد يعود كومباني إلى مقاعد البدلاء في مباراة الدوري الألماني ضد كولن في 20 نوفمبر الجاري. وبع…

title: Open-source GPU task manager reveals exactly what's eating your VRAM
summary: A new open-source GitHub project called gputaskman has been released by Microsoft VP Scott Hanselman.
body: Microsoft VP Scott Hanselman has revealed a new open-source GitHub project called gputaskman . The name neatly encapsulates the headline role of this tool, a GPU-focused task manager, but its scope might be broader than you expect. This new tool for Windows, Linux, and macOS can show per-process GPU usage, VRAM consumption , active runtimes, and many more stats. It also breaks out AI/LLM task-specific information. There's a lot going on in my GPU. I'm making a GPU Taskman to get insights to where my GPU memory is going. title: PC's with 64GB of RAM plummet 18% as memory prices soar
summary: CPU-Z data reveals PC memory capacity is dropping for the first time ever. Driven by skyrocketing AI DRAM prices, 64GB RAM adoption plummeted 18% YoY.
body: The latest CPU-Z hardware survey data shows 32GB and 64GB memory configurations down 2.5% and 18% year on year, respectively. The driving factor is no mystery: High-capacity memory has become a luxury in modern PC builds. The AI rush is still gobbling up the global DRAM supply, so prices for the best RAM options across DDR4 and DDR5 have gone through the roof. If you are not familiar with CPU-Z, it is a free program that gives you a detailed breakdown of the hardware inside your system. It only tracks systems where it is actually installed and running, so it does not report monthly retail sales figures. Do not take the data as sales figures in any sense. They represent CPU-Z's active user base. 32GB and 16GB are common configurations that have grown over the years. According to the gathered data, 32GB configurations lead CPU-Z's user base with a 37.2% share, with 16GB configurations close behind at 33%. Not a surprise, really, since applications and games have grown more memory-intensive. 16GB has been the baseline for a long time now, and 32GB is now the sweet spot for many people, even gamers. title: Homelabber uses second-gen Optane memory sticks to run a 2.8-trillion-parameter AI model on CPU alone
summary: A Reddit homelab user ran Moonshot AI’s 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 CPU-only on Optane PMem 200 at 0.85 tokens/s with a 1-bit quant.
body: A homelab builder on Reddit has run Moonshot AI’s 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 AI model on discontinued second-gen Optane PMem 200 memory, using a 40-core 3rd-gen Xeon Scalable CPU and not a GPU for inference. The build runs hot, and the builder’s advice is that you “treat active DIMM cooling as mandatory,” with dual 12W blower fans aimed at the modules to get temperatures under control. The project, a follow-up to a separate user’s first-gen Optane build earlier this year, runs at a sluggish 0.85 tokens per second even with 1-bit quantization. Using secondhand Optane, instead, is one of the few ways to reach that capacity at home. It doesn’t help that DRAM prices have skyrocketed , and the builder says the Optane memory costs “a fraction” of the equivalent. title: Pocket-sized Ukrainian receiver intercepts Russian strike drone video feeds up to six miles away
summary: The D·Vision SDR can intercept signals from 500 MHz to 8.7 GHz, covering the 4.1-4.5 GHz spectrum that Russian Molniya strike drones use to communicate with their operators.
body: CODE380, a radio manufacturer based in Kyiv, just built a new software-defined radio (SDR) that intercepts analog video signals that Russian drones transmit to their operators, making it easier for troops to find and intercept them. According to Defense News, the D·Vision SDR can sweep radio frequencies from 500 MHz to 8.7 GHz and convert any intercepted analog radio signal into a video feed. It has a detection range of up to six miles for signals on the 540 MHz to 6 GHz band, and up to two to three miles for higher frequencies. Although this isn’t the first passive Ukraine-made drone detector, it’s one of the lightest models produced so far, weighing just 10 ounces or 290 grams — by comparison, an iPhone 18 Pro Max weighs about 8.78 ounces or 249 grams. Its competitors include the Vydun 7.5, which weighs around 2 pounds or 900 grams and could intercept signals at up to 7.5 GHz; the 23-ounce (650-gram) Chuyka 3.0, which can detect signals at up to 8.8 GHz; and the SENSE-4, which weighs 21 ounces or 600 grams and could detect drone signals of up to 8.2 GHz. title: WoW: Forever launch used 70,480 CPU cores and 251 terabytes of RAM
summary: Inside the astonishing hardware behind World of Warcraft: Forever. 251TB of RAM and 70K cores kept millions of players online without a hitch.
body: Blizzard pulled out all the stops to ensure World of Warcraft: Forever survived a chaotic launch night. What was the company's secret weapon? Splurging an absurd amount of money on infrastructure made up of 3,924 virtual machines with 70,480 CPU cores and a whopping 251,136 GB, or 251 TB, of memory. Praised by media and players as one of the smoothest launches in Blizzard's history, World of Warcraft: Forever requires significant computing firepower. 3,924 virtual machines work out to 18 cores and 64GB of memory per instance. body: Eight years after GlobalFoundries abandoned the development of its 7nm FinFET technology, the company is preparing to return to 7nm-class performance, this time by going via a different route. Its FDX Fusion process, built on FD-SOI (fully depleted silicon-on-insulator) technology, promises 7nm-class performance using advanced planar transistors, with no EUV lithography necessary. In an interview with Tom's Hardware Premium , GlobalFoundries' Sudipto Bose, vice president of the FD-SOI business unit, shared new details about its FDX Fusion technology, including its 8nm-class logic density, advanced planar transistors, manufacturing costs, and plans to begin commercial production in 2028. The company also explained how it intends to compete with conventional FinFET technologies and why it believes FD-SOI has a future beyond the 22nm-class generation. I was able to get about five feet away from my subject in a harsh RF environment. I didn’t test it further than that, so it may go farther. body: A Pat Gelsinger-backed Georgia Tech spinout, Nagare Labs, says its Z2RAM can put SRAM-speed memory , at DRAM density, directly on top of AI chips. The founders’ own papers show a fast-improving cell that, tested up to 85 degrees Celsius, holds data for over 300 seconds. Gen 1 is projected to have 5x SRAM density with six stacked layers, 14x DRAM speed, and 3x less read energy than SRAM. AI chips require a lot of bandwidth, and it has been challenging to get sufficient yields of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to feed them. Even when manufacturers can get it, some reportedly plan to settle for fewer layers for yield reasons, and heat is another. Heat is also why Samsung’s zHBM , which stacks DRAM directly on the processor, is planned at only about four layers. Alternatives include high-bandwidth flash , still in development, which stacks NAND like HBM and would sit beside the GPU, or SRAM stacked directly on the die, which is less dense and more expensive for the capacity, but also faster. DRAM, which is more capacious, can sit on top of the compute, but heat limits how hard the logic underneath can run. That limit is already shaping chipmakers’ design path for stacked memory. title: Combined OpenSSH and musl-libc flaws let anyone into Alpine Linux and other distros by typing anything over 256 characters as a password
summary: Combined OpenSSH and musl-libc flaws let anyone into Alpine Linux and other distros by typing anything over 256 characters as a password
body: The internet is still reeling from the PHP engine vulnerability and all other security vulnerabilities found over the past few weeks, and we're not done. Today's special is quite spicy: you can get into Alpine, OpenWRT, and other Linux distros without needing a password, thanks to a combined bug with OpenSSH and musl libc. Just randomly type over 256 characters on the password prompt and you'll be let in through the SSHhole . It works if you set an empty password for system users, which is the default on multiple distros. The bug is present, though not necessarily enabled, across Buildroot, Yocto, and Void Linux. OpenWRT uses Dropbear for authentication by default, but users can install OpenSSH instead. The largest concern is by far Alpine, though, as it's pretty much the default choice for what could amount to millions of installs across Docker/Kubernetes/Proxmox containers and endless dependencies thereof, servers, cloud VMs, and embedded devices, among many others. Alpine comes with the requisite conditions set and password authentication enabled by default, which is why it needs immediate patching.
